quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: You operate the rear brake of a motorcycle with your right foot.

questions.question: Which item gives the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective riding gear?

options.text: Boots that go above the ankle

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a leather jacket, sturdy pants, boots that cover your ankles, and hearing protection. Soft pants do not protect you.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your eyes and face.
questions.explanation: A face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Sunglasses are not enough protection. In Vermont, you are not required to wear eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You should sound your horn to make the driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: You can only pass another vehicle where it is safe and legal to do so. Both the start and finish of the pass must be in a passing zone.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat big enough for two riders.
Only have one set of footrests.
Not require your passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat big enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle has a seat for two. Your motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear you do.

questions.question: Several things affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Which does NOT affect it?
questions.correctAnswerText: Height
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration depends on how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect it.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on a good surface, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then apply it again quickly.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on a good surface, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what does the lead rider mean when they raise their left arm and point with one finger?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single line.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders in a group communicate. When the lead rider raises their left arm and points with one finger, it means the group should form a single line.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. The left tire track is often the safest option.

questions.question: Which is NOT a check you need to do before riding?

options.text: Test both brakes to make sure the brake light turns on.
Check that the paint is not scratched.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the paint is not scratched.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire pressure and condition, oil and fluid levels, and that all lights work: headlight, taillight, signal lights, and brake light.

questions.question: What is dangerous about riding next to a car?

options.text: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
It is only a problem on wet roads.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle puts you in their blind spot. The vehicle also blocks your escape route.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard to see at night. What should you do?

options.text: Ride directly in front of another vehicle so their headlights show you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use the lights ahead of you to see the road. Turn on your high beam headlight unless you are following or meeting another vehicle. Be ready to change your lane position.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders be?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front. This lets experienced riders in the back watch and help them.

questions.question: If there are hazards on your left, which part of the lane should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: The right portion.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before riding it. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: What is true about a motorcycle horn?

options.text: Other drivers usually cannot hear it.
It can get someone's attention quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can get someone's attention quickly.
questions.explanation: Your horn can be useful to get attention. However, motorcycle horns are not as loud as car horns, so drivers may not hear you. Never rely only on your horn to handle a hazard.

questions.question: What should passengers do while riding?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with the driver.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you during turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What is true about most motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They are caused by worn tires.
They happen at speeds above 55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience. Most crashes happen during the day at low speeds.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may drive slowly while looking for a spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver may pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: If a driver is following you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before you slow down to warn them.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down. A tailgater may be focused on you and not see hazards ahead that require slowing down.

questions.question: What should your helmet do to give you the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Meet Department of Transportation guidelines.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious defects.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Any time you plan to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you plan to turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.
questions.correctAnswerText: Five times
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: What lessens the effects of alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver processes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time allows your body to remove alcohol.

questions.question: When is it important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than larger vehicle brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing in unexpected places, such as mid-block or near an alley.

questions.question: Your lane position should NOT:

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Invite other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position keeps you safe by staying out of blind spots, helping you see and be seen, avoiding hazards, and giving you an escape route. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You may finish the pass in a no passing zone if you started before it began.
You may exceed the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be completed at or below the posted speed limit and only in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller, so you can't see as much.
Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. You cannot rely only on mirrors to see what is behind you. Frequent head checks should be part of your normal routine.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Give you a poor view of road hazards.
Allow others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that lets you see others and lets them see you. Stay out of another driver's blind spot.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
Get other friends to talk them out of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to talk them out of riding.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone who has been drinking to ride. Do everything you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help convince them not to ride.

questions.question: A face shield should:

options.text: Give you a clear view to both sides.
Block all air from passing through it.
Be tight enough to prevent glasses from fitting under it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear side views, fasten securely, let air pass through, and leave room for glasses if needed.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Not use the brakes, but downshift instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes when you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When you are being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the left part of the lane.
Ride in the right part of the lane.
Ride in any part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind, stay in the center of your lane. This discourages the other driver from moving back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take only a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Inspect your motorcycle before every ride. A thorough inspection usually takes just a few minutes.

questions.question: When you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the left part of the lane.
Ride in the right part of the lane.
Move between the three parts of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases your crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to move back too soon.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Be worn only during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials all the time to be more visible.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have very small blind spots that are not a concern.
Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a regular part of your scanning.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees they will yield to you.
Does not mean they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver sees you. A driver can look directly at you and still not notice you are there.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or anxiety can make you drowsy. This can make it unsafe to ride. Before riding, know how any medication affects you.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, clothing:

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not cover your arms or legs completely.
Should not include a jacket if the weather is warm.
Can provide protection in the event of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can provide protection in the event of a crash.
questions.explanation: The right clothing protects you if you crash. Always wear a jacket and long pants that cover your arms and legs, even in warm weather. Clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that you cannot move.

questions.question: Riding with a passenger:

options.text: Usually results in no difference in handling a motorcycle.
Is usually safe for beginning riders.
Can affect the handling of a motorcycle.
Is encouraged to get operators used to different riding situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect the handling of a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are used for road rules like speed limits. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless following or meeting another vehicle), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective clothing to be visible. Change your lane position as needed to see better, be seen, and have space to react.

questions.question: Which of the following is not protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sandals
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves when riding.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across the surface.
Tighten your grip on the handlebars and speed up to get past the hazard.
Ride on the shoulder instead of on the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across the surface.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging to correct the weaving is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should travel:

options.text: More slowly than you would during the day under similar conditions.
At the speed you would travel during the day under similar conditions.
Faster than you would during the day under similar conditions.
On the shoulder of the road so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than you would during the day under similar conditions.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day in similar weather and traffic. It is harder to see hazards in the dark. Riding slower helps you avoid hazards.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, oil, and metal plates in the road have poor traction. Dry pavement has good traction.

questions.question: When riding, a cushion of space is helpful to:

options.text: Give you space to react to hazards.
Allow you to look at road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you space to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Keep a cushion of space around your motorcycle. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need space to maneuver safely.
